ideas.truth: Diwali mithai-buying in an old bazaar like Johari Bazaar runs on trust passed between generations — the box is a promise, not just a snack.
ideas.moment: The instant the shopkeeper ties the box shut, with the free extra pieces visibly pressed in on top before the lid closes.
ideas.key_frame: Overhead close-up of a kaju katli box being hand-tied with red-gold thread, diyas glowing at the frame edges, free 250g pieces stacked visibly on top.

ideas.truth: Nobody buys mithai for themselves at Diwali — they buy it to look generous when they hand it over, and a free extra makes the giver look even more generous for the same spend.
ideas.moment: The moment of gifting — a hand extends a stacked plate of kaju katli toward the viewer, as if the viewer is the one receiving it.
ideas.key_frame: A hand offering an overflowing thali of kaju katli diamonds toward camera, warm diya bokeh behind, one open space on the plate for copy.

ideas.truth: In a bazaar of jewelers, a shopkeeper's morning stack of fresh mithai is itself the entire sales pitch — nobody needs to be told it's fresh when it's built to catch the light like jewellery.
ideas.moment: The first hour after the kaju katli is cut and stacked — laid into a small glinting pyramid on brass, with a visibly separate bonus mound beside it, before the day's crowd arrives.
ideas.key_frame: A glowing pyramid of diamond-cut kaju katli on a brass thali, silver-leaf edges catching sharp highlight, with a distinctly separate, slightly smaller mound of extra pieces placed just in front of the main stack — visually reading as the bonus quantity — diyas flanking the base, calm dark space above for the headline.

why: No photos were supplied and this is a single static poster (duration 0) for a fast scroll — idea 3 needs no invented people or gestures, plays the Johari-Bazaar-jewelers pun straight into the product's own diamond-cut shape, and — with the added bonus-mound detail — now shows the 'extra 250g' offer in the image itself, not only in overlay text, giving Ogilvy's 'one visual shock, promise shown in the picture' the cleanest possible canvas.
treatment: A single warm, glowing image: a brass thali stacked into a small pyramid of diamond-cut kaju katli, each piece edged in a thin silver-leaf sheen, catching soft golden light from two diyas placed just behind on either side, with faint out-of-focus rangoli colour in a deep-maroon background. Just in front of the main pyramid sits a distinctly separate, slightly smaller mound of extra kaju katli pieces — visually reading as the bonus quantity a buyer gets free, so the offer is legible even with the sound off and before the eye reaches the text. The stack is lit the way Johari Bazaar's own jewellers light a display case — sharp highlights, rich shadow, no clutter, nothing photographed, nothing borrowed. Above the thali, a calm dark-maroon band holds the Hindi headline; below, a narrower calm band holds the offer line and the shop's name and address. One product, one light, one promise — dressed exactly as generous and festive as the occasion demands, and nothing else competing for the eye.

scenes.prompt: An Instagram and WhatsApp Status festive sweet-shop poster: a small pyramid of fresh diamond-cut kaju katli, each piece edged with a thin silver-leaf sheen, stacked on a polished brass thali, with a distinctly separate, slightly smaller mound of extra kaju katli pieces placed just in front of the main pyramid — clearly reading as a bonus portion on the same thali. Two lit clay diyas glow softly on either side, warm golden light catching the glossy cut edges against a deep-maroon backdrop with soft out-of-focus rangoli colour dots. Photoreal festive product-photography style, high colour saturation, strong highlights, clean unmarked surfaces. Leave a calm dark band across the top third for a Hindi headline, and a calm narrower band across the bottom third for offer and shop-name text.
on_screen_copy: 1 kg kaju katli pe 250 g FREE
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: Same framing as the main prompt: the glowing brass-thali pyramid of diamond-cut kaju katli fully stacked and lit, with its separate bonus mound already in place beside it, diyas already glowing on either side, calm top and bottom bands empty and ready for text overlay.
scenes.S1_feeling: Warm festive desire — a want to buy or gift this right now.
scenes.S2_first_frame: The glowing pyramid of kaju katli on brass, plus its visibly separate bonus mound, already fully stacked and lit — the idea of fresh abundance and a generous extra is complete on arrival, with nothing left for motion to build.
scenes.S3_one_action: None — static image. The only 'action' is the viewer's eye moving from the lit stack, to the smaller bonus mound beside it, up to the headline and down to the offer, inside a single glance (under 1 second on a scroll).
scenes.S4_new_information: The viewer learns the specific offer (250g free on 1kg) and exactly where to buy it (Johari Bazaar, Jaipur) — the quantity of the bonus is now also suggested visually by the separate mound, with the exact numbers confirmed by text.
scenes.S5_impact: The jewel-like shine on the sweets, and the visibly separate bonus mound, both have to register as 'fresh and generous' even as a muted thumbnail on Status — the payoff is visual richness large enough to survive a small phone screen.

finish.copy_placement: दिवाली धमाका set large in Devanagari in the calm top-third band; 1 kg kaju katli pe 250 g FREE directly below it in the bottom-third band, with Shree Ganesh Sweets and Johari Bazaar Jaipur set smaller beneath the offer line, all added by code — nothing is drawn by the image model.
finish.end_card: The single frame itself is the end card: the lit kaju katli pyramid with its bonus mound, headline, offer, and shop name/location all visible at once — no separate closing frame, since this is a static poster.
finish.music: Not applicable — static image for WhatsApp Status/Instagram, no audio bed required.

decisions.D1_idea: The exact moment fresh kaju katli is stacked into a jeweller's-worthy pyramid on a brass thali, with a visibly separate bonus mound beside it, lit like the display cases of Johari Bazaar itself — making 'fresh,' 'generous,' and the extra-quantity offer all visible without relying only on words.
decisions.D2_conflict: Every mithai shop's Diwali poster claims 'fresh' and 'pure' with the same recycled diya-and-rangoli visuals, so shoppers scroll past nearly all of them.
decisions.D3_roles: Hero: the Diwali shopper in Johari Bazaar choosing where to buy a gift-worthy box. Brand: Shree Ganesh Sweets as the guide that makes the choice visibly generous and correct, offering the extra 250g as what a discerning buyer picks — not a discount for the cash-strapped. (No customer figure is shown, per the brief's 'no photos' instruction — the hero's choice is represented by the product itself.)
decisions.D4_opening: A bold, glowing stack of diamond-cut kaju katli on brass with its bonus mound, lit like jewellery — the whole image, since this is a still, not a video mid-action.
decisions.D5_brand: Shop name and location appear once, as text laid in by code in the bottom band; the product visual itself (invented kaju katli stack + bonus mound) is the only recurring asset since no logo or photo was supplied.
decisions.D6_ask_and_end: Ask: come to Shree Ganesh Sweets in Johari Bazaar this Diwali, carried by text (shop name + location) and the implicit urgency of a festival-dated offer. End frame: the product itself, glowing, with headline and offer overlaid — default kept.
decisions.D7_product_truth: It is kaju katli (customer words); shop is Shree Ganesh Sweets, Johari Bazaar, Jaipur (customer words); offer is 1kg + 250g free (customer words); diamond-cut shape and silver-leaf finish are the standard, honest visual convention for kaju katli, invented per the brief's instruction to invent the look since no photo was supplied. The bonus quantity is now also shown visually as a separate mound, not only stated in text. No taste, ingredient, or purity claims are shown, per the 'cut defensive reassurances' note.
decisions.D8_deviations: No photos supplied, so the product look is invented once and used once (single still, duration 0), removing the multi-scene consistency problem entirely. Not using retro filmi-poster styling, since that craft note flags it as dated to urban audiences — going instead for a clean, high-saturation jewel-lit product shot. Not depicting any shopkeeper or customer, since the customer asked only for 'no photos' and the product to look fresh — adding people would be an unrequested addition; the 'hero' role (C03) and 'tension' (C02) are therefore carried structurally, not pictorially, and are flagged as accepted trade-offs in the checklist rather than solved by adding unrequested content.
